blocks.h2: Types of Water Filtration We Install
blocks.intro: The right system depends on what's in your water and what you want to change:

tiles.body: Filters all the water entering the house, for taste, odor, chlorine and sediment at every tap.
Removes the minerals that cause hard water, scale on fixtures and buildup in water heaters and pipes.
Filtered drinking and cooking water at the kitchen sink.
Protects fixtures and appliances from grit and particles, especially in homes with older pipes.

bodies: Testing comes first. Before we recommend any system, we check your water for hardness and the other things that affect taste, scale and your plumbing. That way you pay for the system your water actually needs, not the most expensive one on the truck.

Testing is also worth doing when something changes: a new taste or smell, staining on fixtures, or scale building up faster than it used to. If a water heater failed early, hard water may have played a part, and testing tells you if a softener would protect the next one.

blocks.h2: Water Treatment in Older Highland Park Homes
blocks.intro: Nearly half of Highland Park homes were built before 1960. Older plumbing can affect your water as much as the water supply does.

items.body: Older galvanized water lines corrode from the inside, which can cause rust-colored water and grit at faucets. A sediment filter helps, but the long-term fix may be the pipes. See [leak repairs](/highland-park/leak-repairs).
Scale from hard water builds up in tank and tankless heaters and shortens their life. A softener can protect a new heater. See [water heater installation](/highland-park/water-heater-installation).

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton

steps.body: We test your water and show you the results before recommending anything.

blocks.h2: Water Filtration Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: Do I need a water softener or a filter?
items.preview: A softener handles hard water. A filter handles taste, odor and sediment. Testing tells you which.
items.answer: They do different things. A softener removes the minerals that cause hard water and scale. A filter removes things that affect taste, odor or clarity, like chlorine and sediment. Testing tells us which one, or both, makes sense for your home.

items.q: How do I know if I have hard water?
items.preview: White spots, scale on fixtures and poor lather are common signs. A test gives the number.
items.answer: Signs include white spots on dishes and glass, scale on faucets and showerheads, soap that doesn't lather well and a water heater that rumbles. A water test gives you the actual number.

items.q: How often do filters need to be changed?
items.preview: It depends on the system. We'll give you the schedule for yours.
items.answer: It depends on the system and how much water you use. Some cartridges last a few months, others a year or more. We'll tell you the schedule for the system you choose.

items.q: How much does a water filtration system cost?
items.preview: It depends on the system and install. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the system type, whole-home or point-of-use, and the install. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
